title: Create a "Cohort Icebreaker" Content Pack
description: To drive engagement, bootcamps need activities. Write a set of structured prompts that a bootcamp instructor can post in a Zedu channel on Day 1 to get students talking and using the platform features correctly.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add low-disclosure and asynchronous alternatives to each prompt
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Review the ten day-one prompts and add a voluntary low-disclosure option plus an asynchronous way to participate for each, without changing the feature-learning goal. Flag prompts that ask for personal details, add a facilitator note for learners who prefer to observe first, and check that each alternative still practices the intended Zedu feature. Deliver a prompt-to-alternative table, copy-ready variants, and mobile/accessibility checks. This complements the existing prompt pack rather than creating another set of ten.

upvotes.reason: Validates Zedu's technical marketing and cohort operations: Add low-disclosure and asynchronous alternatives to each prompt. Review the ten day-one prompts and add a voluntary low-disclosure option plus an asynchron.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Pair each prompt with the instructor's follow-up reply and a moderation note
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A prompt only works if the instructor keeps it going. For each day-one prompt, add a short model reply the instructor posts after the first answers (to show the expected tone and model the feature being taught), a nudge for quiet learners, and a moderation note on what to do if a reply oversteps, for example personal details or off-topic arguments. Done: the ten prompts each with reply, nudge and moderation note, in a copy-paste format ready for a Zedu channel.

upvotes.reason: "Pair each prompt with the instructor's follow-up reply and a moderation note" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

Instructor follow-up examples and privacy-aware moderation notes make the existing icebreakers easier to run responsibly; nudges should remain optional and avoid pressuring learners to disclose personal information.

This is a practical extension to the approved ten-prompt pack: instructor replies and nudges help the activity continue, while a moderation note helps facilitators handle personal details or off-topic replies. It stays tied to the existing prompts instead of duplicating them.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Plan for the quiet participant: the nudge, the pair-up and the public alternative
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Every cohort has members who read everything and post nothing, and a day-one activity that only rewards public posting teaches them to stay silent. Work: for each prompt, add a low-visibility route to participate (a DM to the instructor, a pair with one other learner, a reply to a pinned summary) and the message the instructor sends to someone who has not posted by day two. Deliver the routes, the nudge wording, and the point at which a quiet learner should be treated as a signal rather than a preference.

upvotes.reason: "Plan for the quiet participant: the nudge, the pair-up and the public alternative" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
Public-posting-only icebreakers teach quiet learners to stay silent. DM, pair-up and reply routes widen participation without forcing exposure, and the day-two nudge is actionable.

An icebreaker pack that only rewards public posting loses the readers who make up most of a cohort. Low-visibility routes, a nudge wording, and the point where quiet becomes a signal address the real audience.

pendingIdeas.title: Add a "skip if" rule per prompt, because cohorts that already know each other resent introductions
pendingIdeas.description: In-service teachers, alumni groups and internal teams do not need name games, and posting one signals that nobody looked at who is in the room. Work: for each prompt, write the condition under which it should be skipped and the substitute that fits a group with existing relationships. Deliver the skip conditions, the substitutes, and the note on how an instructor can tell in the first ten minutes which group they have.

upvotes.reason: "Add a "skip if" rule per prompt, because cohorts that already know each other resent introductions" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Spread the ten prompts across the first week instead of posting them all on day one
pendingIdeas.description: Ten icebreakers in one channel on day one turns the channel into a wall nobody reads. Work: assign each prompt to a day and a purpose (day one: names and one tool; day three: a voice note; day five: a pair task), and state what the instructor does with the answers each time. Deliver the week plan, the reason each prompt sits on its day, and the two prompts that only work after a live session has happened.

pendingIdeas.title: Write each prompt in three modes: text, voice note and photo, because not every learner can do all three
pendingIdeas.description: A prompt that requires typing fast or showing a face excludes the learner who is on a borrowed phone in a shared room. Work: rewrite each activity so it can be completed as text, as a short voice note, or as a photo of something on the desk, with the same teaching purpose in each. Deliver the three-mode table, the prompts where a mode is genuinely unavailable, and the instruction that tells learners they may choose.

upvotes.reason: "Write each prompt in three modes: text, voice note and photo, because not every learner can do all three" has a defined audience and a clear done-state, and it addresses something the site does not currently say. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
Borrowed phones in shared rooms are normal for part of Zedu's audience, and a prompt that needs typing speed or a face excludes them. Three modes with the same teaching purpose keeps the pack usable.

pendingIdeas.title: Write the debrief, so the answers become a pinned summary rather than ten forgotten posts
pendingIdeas.description: Icebreakers produce content that disappears down the channel by day three, and the group loses the useful part: who does what. Work: define what the instructor collects from the answers (skills, time zones, what people want help with), how it is summarised into one pinned post, and how it is used in the first project grouping. Deliver the summary template, the grouping rule, and the one privacy question (what a learner may not want repeated) that the instructor must ask first.

Without a pinned summary the useful output (skills, time zones, who can help) disappears down the channel. Tying the debrief to project grouping gives it a second job.
